newsitem.title: UK: SEDGWICK H1 SEEN FLAT AS COMPETITION BITES.
newsitem.headline: SEDGWICK H1 SEEN FLAT AS COMPETITION BITES.

text.p: British insurance broker Sedgwick Group is expected to struggle to match last year's figures when it posts results for the first half next Tuesday.
Like UK rival Willis Corroon which unveiled a sharp drop in profits when it reported earlier this week, keen competition and the strength of the pound are both likely to take their toll.

Sterling wiped 6.6 million pounds ($10.5 million) off Willis' profits in the first half and competition showed little sign of easing especially in the U.S. market and some global speciality businesses.
Last year Sedgwick reported first half profits of 64.1 million pounds. Analysts are forecasting this year's to range between 61 and 67 million pounds with a number toward the lower end of that band.

Sedgwick's operational strategy has been geared at lessening the group's dependence on the underwriting cycle by increasing fee-earning consultancy business. It has also concentrated on broadening its business base and keeping a tight control of costs.
Nevertheless, first quarter profits slipped four percent in the first quarter to 43.5 million pounds as the rise in the currency knocked 3.4 million pounds off the figures.
Underlying brokerage, however, grew by three percent.
Sedgwick said then that it was looking to extend worldwide consultancy and outsourcing activities and for new initiatives aimed at additional profit improvement and cost containment.
Employee benefit revenues, currently around one quarter of the total, are expected to grow as Sedgwick Noble Lowndes increases penetration and develops new markets.
About 13 percent of property casualty brokerage is on a fee basis.
The company also aims to continue with small, add on purchases particularly in continental Europe.

Lurking in the background at Sedgwick has been persistent speculation that a tie-up with Willis could provide the two companies with a solution to the problems posed by the intense competition and slim margins.
Both have played down the suggestion but some argue something dramatic is needed to close the gap with U.S. rivals Aon and Marsh & Mclennan .
News that David Herro, the Chicago based investor responsible for a shareholder revolt at Saatchi & Saatchi, has a three percent stake in the group further fuelled the rumour mill back in April.
Herro, who ousted Maurice Saatchi as chairman of the advertising group has, however, insisted the investment in Sedgwick is passive. ($ = 0.628 British Pounds)
